t: Largest Local Values in a Matrix II
o: Each non-zero cell with value x inspects the square of radius x around it, except the four corner cells (where both row and column offsets equal x); it is a local maximum if none of the inspected cells exceeds x. Example 3: x = 1 regions are the cell plus orthogonal neighbors, so all five 1s qualify. A naive per-cell scan costs O(x^2) per cell — up to ~1.6e9 operations on a 200x200 all-200 matrix, so we need fast rectangular max queries. The square-minus-four-corners region decomposes exactly into three rectangles, answerable with a 2D sparse table.
k: The ignored cells are only the four diagonal corners of the radius-x square (|dr| = x AND |dc| = x).
Square minus 4 corners = middle vertical band (full rows, inner columns) plus two narrow side strips.
A 2D sparse table answers any rectangle max in O(1) after O(nm log n log m) preprocessing.

a.i: For every non-zero cell, iterate over its clamped radius-x square, skipping the four corners, and verify no value exceeds x. Direct translation of the definition; correct but potentially too slow on dense large-valued matrices.
s: For each non-zero cell (i, j) with value x, loop r over [i-x, i+x] and c over [j-x, j+x] clamped to the grid.
Skip cells with |r-i| == x and |c-j| == x.
If any visited value exceeds x, the cell fails; otherwise count it.
a.t: O(n * m * x^2) worst case (~1.6e9 for a dense 200x200 matrix of 200s) — may TLE

a.n: Approach 2: 2D Sparse Table over Three Rectangles (Optimal)
a.i: Precompute a 2D sparse table for range-max queries. The inspection region (square minus corners) is exactly the union of: full-height band with inner columns [j-x+1, j+x-1], plus rows [i-x+1, i+x-1] crossed with column j-x, plus the same rows with column j+x. Three O(1) max queries per cell give the region maximum; the cell qualifies iff that max is <= x.
s: Build a 2D sparse table st[a][b][i][j] = max of the 2^a x 2^b block at (i, j).
Write a query(r1,r2,c1,c2) combining the four overlapping power-of-two blocks.
For each non-zero cell, take the max of the three covering rectangles (clamped, skipping empty ones).
Count the cell if the region max <= its value.
a.t: O(nm log n log m) preprocessing + O(nm) queries — comfortably fast for 200x200
a.sp: O(nm log n log m) for the sparse table (~10 MB here)

w: Always confirm the ignored cells are exactly the four corners — misreading 'within x rows and columns' is the top pitfall. Zero cells are never local maximums regardless of neighbors. Equal values are fine (only strictly greater neighbors disqualify), which is why example 4 yields 4. In an interview, describe the brute force, then the rectangle decomposition plus sparse table; a sliding-window/deque alternative exists only when x is fixed globally. Follow-up: report the positions, or handle streaming matrix updates.
